So we need Fed data, maybe from Federal Reserve's "Household Debt" or "Households' Credit and Spending" or "Household Debt and Credit Report" (HDC). The Fed releases "Household Debt and Credit Report" on a quarterly basis. It includes a table of debt-to-income ratio by metropolitan statistical area (MSA). We need to focus on MSAs that are partially or entirely within New Jersey. So list of MJAs: New York-Newark-Jersey City, NJ sections? Let's think.

Metropolitan Statistical Areas that include New Jersey: there are "New York-Newark-Jersey City, NY-NJ-PA" (includes parts of New Jersey). "Harrisburg-Lancaster-Middletown, PA" - not NJ. "Philadelphia" etc. "Greenville, SC" etc. There's also "Newark" MSA? Let's search for list. So we need MSA name, debt-to-income ratio range (like 1.20-1.35?) Actually "extends to 1.35 or higher" means the upper bound of the estimated range is >= 1.35.

Thus we need to find, for Q1 2023, the table of MSAs with debt-to-income ratio estimate ranges (likely "Between 1.14 and 1.20" etc). The Fed's report has a column "Estimated Debt-to-Income Ratio" with range like 1.23-1.26? I'm not sure.

## EFA: Household Debt
### Household Debt Overview
A growing body of research documents the importance of household debt to the Great Recession and subsequent sluggish recovery. Notably, counties in which households were heavily indebted relative to their income at the beginning of the downturn experienced sharper declines in consumption expenditure and employment. The tables and interactive maps below allow users to explore the ratio of debt to income by state, metropolitan statistical area, and county for each year since 1999. Household debt is calculated from FRBNY Consumer Credit Panel/Equifax Data, and household income is reported by the Bureau of Labor Statistics. For more information see the associated FEDS Note. Please note that the precise data values are not available for download and that the value ranges in the data files correspond to the color-coded scales used in the interactive map.

# Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System _The Federal Reserve, the central bank of the United States, provides the nation with a safe, flexible, and stable monetary and financial system._
## EFA: Household Debt
### Household Debt Overview
A growing body of research documents the importance of household debt to the Great Recession and subsequent sluggish recovery. Notably, counties in which households were heavily indebted relative to their income at the beginning of the downturn experienced sharper declines in consumption expenditure and employment. The tables and interactive maps below allow users to explore the ratio of debt to income by state, metropolitan statistical area, and county for each year since 1999. Household debt is calculated from FRBNY Consumer Credit Panel/Equifax Data, and household income is reported by the Bureau of Labor Statistics. For more information see the associated FEDS Note. Please note that the precise data values are not available for download and that the value ranges in the data files correspond to the color-coded scales used in the interactive map.

## EFA: Household Debt
### Household Debt Overview
A growing body of research documents the importance of household debt to the Great Recession and subsequent sluggish recovery. Notably, counties in which households were heavily indebted relative to their income at the beginning of the downturn experienced sharper declines in consumption expenditure and employment. The tables and interactive maps below allow users to explore the ratio of debt to income by state, metropolitan statistical area, and county for each year since 1999. Household debt is calculated from FRBNY Consumer Credit Panel/Equifax Data, and household income is reported by the Bureau of Labor Statistics. For more information see the associated FEDS Note. Please note that the precise data values are not available for download and that the value ranges in the data files correspond to the color-coded scales used in the interactive map.

# Enhanced Financial Accounts: Household Debt
Board of Governors
A growing body of research documents the importance of household debt to the Great Recession and subsequent sluggish recovery. Notably, counties in which households were heavily indebted relative to their income at the beginning of the downturn experienced sharper declines in consumption expenditure and employment. The tables and interactive maps allow users to explore the ratio of debt to income by state, metropolitan statistical area, and county for each year since 1999.

Industrial production and capacity utilization data for April 2023 are now available.
